records.name: Relâche
records.summary: A music ensemble that presents concerts and collaborative projects, and invites singers and players to join some performances.
records.what_you_do: Attend a listed concert, or take part in a public project such as Unsilent Night, which the group says anyone can join. Multi-week collaborative workshops are also listed.

schedule.text: No regular weekly schedule is published. Concerts and projects are listed one at a time.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the site. The Unsilent Night walk is free.

access.notes: The Unsilent Night walk is over 30 minutes long and crosses city streets. The site gives no other access details.

first_step.how: Come to Unsilent Night on Friday, Dec 18, 2026 at 6 pm, a free walk around Rittenhouse Square, or email director@relache.org to ask about performing in a project.
first_step.basis: The Unsilent Night listing says anyone can take part and needs no tickets. The site describes no join or audition process for performers, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Unsilent Night is a group performance of about 45 minutes, on foot through the streets around Rittenhouse Square. Each participant plays one of four digital tracks on a phone or device with speakers, and organizers help you download it before the countdown. Re | UNITE, the group's October concert at the Philadelphia Ethical Society, is ticketed and the site shows no price.
first_visit_tips: Bring a phone or other device with speakers for the Unsilent Night track.
Plan for more than 30 minutes of walking, including crossing city streets.
Buy Re | UNITE tickets through the ticket link on the group's site before the Oct 25 concert.

records.notes: Three listed events: Re | UNITE on Oct 25, 2026 (Philadelphia Ethical Society, ticketed), Unsilent Night on Dec 18, 2026 (Rittenhouse Square, free), and Re | OPEN on Jun 6, 2027. No past dated item was found, so status is probably_active. The homepage lists Re | ROOT as January to February 2007, which looks like a typo, so it is not used. The support page footer shows a web designer's personal address; not recorded. The about page says the ensemble began as a composers' collective in 1977 and as an ensemble in 1979. The Wildflower Lab workshop with Wildflower Composers is named on the site (see leads_only). The site has no join, audition or rehearsal page.

records.name: Rev UP Philly
records.summary: A monthly open meeting for people working to make Philadelphia better for people with disabilities and seniors. Residents, workers and organizations come together online to plan change.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly video meeting, share ideas, and sign up to help with disability and senior issues across the city.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on a Wednesday from 3 to 4:30 pm, held on Zoom

access.notes: The event page gives no notes on captions, ASL or interpreters for the meeting. The group's site has an accessibility statement and names the Mid-Atlantic ADA Center for ADA help.

first_step.how: Fill in the short Google sign-up form linked from the event page, then join the next monthly Zoom meeting.
first_step.basis: The event page says the meeting is open to anyone interested in change for people with disabilities and seniors in Philadelphia, and it gives a clear sign-up form. It does not say newcomers are specifically welcome, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: The meeting is a video call on Zoom that runs about an hour and a half on a Wednesday afternoon. Residents, workers and organizations share ideas for changes that matter to people with disabilities and seniors in the city. The event page does not describe the agenda in detail.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the sign-up form on the event page before the meeting.
You need a computer, tablet or phone with internet access to join the Zoom call.
The coalition has its own join page on the group's site, for people who want to take part beyond one meeting.

records.notes: The group's calendar feed holds one entry, the Feb 18, 2026 meeting, and no later meeting is listed. Confirm the next meeting date before a first visit. The Zoom link and passcode on the event page are not recorded here. The event page does not state a price; the Free rating is carried over from tier 1. The coalition join page is separate from the monthly meeting. Disability Pride Pennsylvania is the host organization (see leads_only).

records.name: Revolution Shakespeare
records.summary: A Philadelphia company that puts on Shakespeare in new forms, including adaptations, readings and digital work, with a focus on how audiences hear and learn from the plays.
records.what_you_do: Watch its productions, which have included free outdoor shows in city parks, or follow its readings and digital programs. To ask about auditions or helping out, email the company, since its site lists no open calls.

locations.label: Mailing address, c/o The Painted Bride Arts Center, Project Space

first_step.how: Email revolutionshakespeare@gmail.com to ask about audition calls or helping out. The newsletter form on the homepage shows a setup note and may not be working.
first_step.basis: The site names no open audition, class or volunteer role. The only ways in are an email address and a newsletter form that may not work, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The company's site lists no open classes, rehearsals or volunteer shifts, so a first step is an email. Its public work is mainly productions, readings and digital programs, and some shows, such as the 2026 Hamlet staged in Clark Park, were free outdoor performances. Ask the company before you come about dates and seating.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site has no event calendar.
The mailing address is c/o The Painted Bride Arts Center, so it is not a place to visit.

records.notes: One search for audition calls or volunteer roles found none current. The newsletter form shows a note reading that it needs a storage option. The education page's newest listing is spring 2021 (an ASAP Partnership program), so no current classes are published. The group's own Hamlet page gives July dates with no year; the Billy Penn article is dated 2026 and is the source for last_sign_of_life. The spring 2026 fundraiser page gives Thursday April 16 with no year, so it is not used as a dated sign of life. The company's fiscal sponsor is The Painted Bride Arts Center; no URL for it was on the pages read, so it is not a lead. Ticket prices for shows are not published.

records.name: Rittenhouse Astronomical Society
records.summary: An astronomy society founded in 1888 that runs public talks with guest speakers and keeps the public posted through a mailing list.
records.what_you_do: Attend a public open house at Ryan Observatory, usually held on the second Saturday evening, or a public night at Columbus Recreation Center in the city. Members get observing nights, workshops and monthly Zoom meetings.

schedule.text: Public open houses at Ryan Observatory fall on the second Saturday of most months, starting at 7:15 pm. Observing nights at the observatory are scheduled around sunset, weather permitting.

locations.label: Ryan Observatory, Muddy Run Park, Holtwood, PA
Columbus Recreation Center, 8th and Wharton, Philadelphia

cost.text: Yearly membership is $50 (Star) or $75 (Supernova), with a $350 Quasar tier. The price of a public open house is not listed.

first_step.how: Come to a public open house at Ryan Observatory on a second Saturday evening. No registration is listed for open houses, and the events page shows the next dates. You can also join the mailing list through the contact page.
first_step.basis: Open houses are listed for all interested people with no registration shown, and the society says no experience is needed to attend (tier 1 read of its about page). Some events are members only.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open houses start at 7:15 pm and run late into the evening, with a talk or themed program at the observatory. Ryan Observatory is in Muddy Run Park in Holtwood, outside the city, so plan your ride. The events page lists no price for open houses.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page the week before, since weather often changes or cancels observing nights.
The observatory is outside the city, so plan transport to Holtwood before you go.
Non-members pay for the beginner telescope workshop; members get it free.

records.notes: Most events are at Ryan Observatory in Muddy Run Park, Holtwood (Lancaster County, outside Philadelphia), with some in Media and Gladwyne. The city events seen were at Columbus Recreation Center (May 22, 2026 and Sep 19, 2026). The verdict stays publish from tier 1, but the owner may want to decide whether a group that mostly meets outside the city counts as serving Philadelphia. Membership: Star $50, Supernova $75 (up to three guests to members only dark-sky events), Quasar $350, all billed yearly. Some events are members or prospective members only. The old rittenhouseastronomicalsociety.org addresses redirect to rasphilly.org. The newsletter sign-up notes that it needs a storage option, so it may not work. The Oct 18, 2026 medal lecture is in Media and needs advance registration.

records.name: Rock to the Future
records.summary: A free music program for young people in under-resourced parts of Philadelphia, run in schools, community centers and the juvenile justice system, with mentoring and college and career help.
records.what_you_do: Join a free music program such as Lyric Lab, a rap and songwriting class for teens that builds toward a live performance. Volunteers and donors can also help.

schedule.text: Lyric Lab meets Mondays from 4 to 6 pm at One Art Community Center. Concert Creators meets Thursdays from 4 to 6 pm at the same site, and Music Production meets Mondays from 6 to 7:30 pm at a second site. Both MusiCore after-school programs meet on weekday afternoons at two schools.

locations.label: As I Plant This Seed (Music Production)

cost.text: Free. Meals, transit passes, and instruments or supplies are provided.

first_step.how: Fill in the program interest form on the Join Now page for Lyric Lab or another program, or call or text 215-302-9633.
first_step.basis: The join page says beginners are welcome, supplies and instruments are provided, and each program has a Sign Up Today button. The MusiCore after-school spots at the two schools are limited to their own students for now, with a waitlist for others.
first_step.what_to_expect: Lyric Lab is a Monday class from 4 to 6 pm at One Art Community Center for teens aged 13 to 19. No experience is needed, and the work builds toward a live performance. Meals, transit passes and instruments are provided at no cost, and a staff member follows up after you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Sign up before you come, using the interest form on the join page.
Check the age range for your program: the songwriting and production classes list ages 13 to 19, and MusiCore lists grades 6 to 12.
Volunteers who work with students must pass PA child abuse and criminal background checks, which can be done free online.

records.notes: The join page names Lyric Lab, Music Production, Concert Creators and two MusiCore after-school sites (Kensington and Germantown). Lyric Lab, Music Production and Concert Creators are open to ages 13 to 19 through the form; the MusiCore sites take current students first and waitlist others. The events page shows no upcoming events, and the group publishes no calendar feed. Volunteer roles cover academic help, music help, mentoring and events support across five neighborhoods. The volunteer page calls the PA child abuse check a clearance and adds an FBI fingerprint check that must be current within 5 years. Newest dated item: the blog post The Joy of Storytelling, Oct 2, 2026. The mailing address on the site is a suite, not a program site.

records.name: Ronnie Vega Memorial People's Fridge at LAVA
records.summary: A food pantry on Lancaster Avenue in West Philadelphia, stocked with leftovers and neighbor donations. It also hosts a monthly free market.
records.what_you_do: Take food at the Monday food share or the Thursday food distro, or come to the second Saturday free market.

schedule.text: Food share every Monday from 3 to 5 pm, food distro every Thursday from 3 to 4 pm, and a free market on the second Saturday from 9 am to noon.

first_step.how: Come to the Monday food share, the Thursday food distro, or the second Saturday free market during the posted hours. The site lists no sign-up, and the only direct contact is the fridge's Instagram page.
first_step.basis: The page says the fridge serves neighbors on posted days and lists no eligibility rules or sign-up, so the way in is clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fridge runs on posted days only: a food share on Monday afternoons, a food distro on Thursday afternoons, and a free market on the second Saturday morning. Stock comes from leftovers from the food distro, other food shares and neighbor donations. The site does not say what to bring or how visits run.
first_visit_tips: Come only during the posted hours, since the site lists no other times.
The site does not say what to bring, so ask the fridge's Instagram page before your first visit if you need to know.

records.notes: LAVA's updates page has no dated posts about the fridge, and its events calendar shows Oct 2026 with no events; the open hours are listed without dates. The newest dated evidence is the citycast article from September 2025, so status stays probably_active. The site does not describe wheelchair access, transit or parking, and gives no phone or email for the fridge. LAVA, the host organization, is a lead.

records.name: Rosenbach Museum & Library
records.summary: A museum and library at 2008 to 2010 Delancey Place that keeps rare books and manuscripts, open for study and for visits to its galleries and programs.
records.what_you_do: Visit the museum and its Treasures Gallery, join a course or public program, or ask about volunteering. Researchers can book appointments to study the collections.

schedule.text: Open Thursday to Saturday 10:30 am to 6 pm and Sunday 10:30 am to 4:30 pm. Closed Monday to Wednesday. Research visits follow different hours and need an appointment.

cost.text: Adults pay $20 for a guided tour or $15 for self-guided. Seniors and students pay less, children aged 12 to 17 pay $10 guided or $7.50 self-guided, and children under 12 get in free. Rosenbach members and AAM, ICOM and NARM members get in free.

access.notes: The south entrance is wheelchair accessible; call 215-732-1600 ext. 110 for help. Service animals are welcome in public areas. The visit page does not mention an elevator, sensory guidance, ASL or captioned tours.

first_step.how: Book a guided or self-guided visit online or by phone at 215-732-1600, or sign up for a public program such as a book club, talk or open house. Volunteer guides apply through the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: Open to the public on posted hours with clear booking links, and several public events are free. The volunteer guide route needs an application, so it is not counted in the rating.
first_step.what_to_expect: Guided tours start at 10:30 am Thursday to Sunday and are booked online. The self-guided option uses the Bloomberg Connects app on your phone, so bring headphones. The museum welcomes photos and notes, though paper notes must be in pencil, and video is not allowed during signature programs.
first_visit_tips: Book ahead by phone or email, since the museum asks visitors to pre-register.
Bring headphones for the self-guided tour, which uses the Bloomberg Connects app.
Use a pencil for notes on paper, and leave food and drink outside the tour.
There is no parking on site, so plan how you will get to Delancey Place.

records.notes: The programs page was longer than one read, so only the public events in its first 100,000 characters (August 2026 to February 2027) were reviewed; no event details are recorded. Volunteer guides complete an eight-week training course, then work three shifts a month, and help with the two open houses and Bloomsday. The volunteer page gives no minimum age. Transit is not described on the visit page. The homepage lists a blog post dated Sept 29, 2026, which is the newest dated item.
